threads.thread_goal: Align on facility layout, zoning, and construction constraints before finalizing design.

messages.text:
Sharing the latest draft of the facility layout and zoning for the new food-grade site for review.

Key points in this version of A3, linked back to the process map in A1 and our scope in T3 and T8:
- Clear separation of raw, processing, and finished goods areas
- Personnel flow with dedicated gowning and handwash points before high-hygiene zones
- Preliminary routing for drainage and HVAC to keep airflow from clean to less clean

I need cross-functional feedback before I freeze this for construction tender:
1) Are the hygiene zones and flows workable from a quality and operations perspective?
2) Any missing control points that should be reflected spatially, based on A1 and T1?
3) From construction side, do the proposed food-grade finishes and drainage slopes look realistic within our budget and T4?

Please flag anything that would block us from meeting the 30-day pilot timeline so we can adjust now rather than later.

Thanks for sharing the update.

From a process and quality flow angle, comparing your zoning with the draft map in A1 and the flow work in T1, a few points:
- Raw material intake: can we add a small sampling room adjacent to the inbound dock, still outside the high-hygiene core, so we do not bring unverified materials deep into the plant?
- High-risk processing: I see the separation, but I am not sure we have enough space for cleaning equipment and chemical storage without encroaching on product areas.
- Finished goods cold storage: the current door placement means outbound pallets will cross near the return of empty crates. That could complicate hygiene.

Before we sign off T3, I would like to see a version where:
1) Sampling and quarantine areas are clearly marked.
2) There is a defined dirty return route for empties that does not intersect with finished goods.

Happy to jump on a quick call if walking through A3 together would help.

Looking at this from inbound and outbound flows, and cross-checking with what we are drafting in T7:

Inbound:
- The raw dock is fine, but we need a clear buffer for temperature checks and document verification before materials move to storage. Could we mark a small inspection bay near the dock, ideally with direct access to the sampling room that was just suggested?

Outbound:
- For finished goods, we should avoid any backtracking of pallets. Right now, the path from cold store to outbound dock crosses the empties return, as already noted. If we can flip the empties corridor to the opposite side of the dock, we keep a one-way flow.

Cold-chain:
- We need space for data logger checks and potential re-cooling if a truck arrives slightly out of spec. A small staging area in front of the cold store would help.

If we can adjust A3 to reflect these, it will make it easier to align T7 and later commissioning checks in A4.

From construction side, I have a couple of concerns before we lock this for T4 and T8.

Materials and finishes:
- You mention food-grade floors and walls, but I do not yet see the exact spec in A3. We need to be precise on floor type, wall coating, and ceiling finish for each zone so I can check availability and cost.
- Drainage slopes look tight in the high-hygiene area. With the current layout, we might struggle to keep the required slope without creating trip hazards.

Schedule and buildability:
- The HVAC routing over the high-hygiene rooms is quite dense. If we do not simplify, it could push commissioning of those rooms and risk the 30-day pilot.

I suggest we:
1) Add a simple table into A3 listing floor, wall, ceiling, and drainage spec per zone, aligned with T8.
2) Run a quick constructability check this week so I can update T4 and A4 accordingly.

I cannot yet confirm we can build this within budget and time until we have that detail.

Looking at the layout with the environmental and biological lens, and anticipating what we will formalize in A5 and T5:

- Airflow: we should ensure that air moves from the cleanest zones to less clean ones. Right now, the HVAC arrows in A3 are not fully clear. Can we mark supply and extract points so we avoid any recirculation from waste or utility areas into production?
- Waste handling: the waste room is adjacent to a personnel corridor that also serves high-hygiene areas. I would prefer a more direct external route for waste to reduce cross-contact risk.
- Sampling and lab space: if we add the sampling room near inbound, we should also consider a small bench for environmental swabs and temporary sample storage.

If we adjust these now, it will be easier to align the monitoring program in T10 and the SOP pack in A6 later on.

Thanks for the detailed comments, very helpful.

On your points:
- Sampling room: I had assumed we could use a corner of the raw storage, but I see the risk. I will add a dedicated sampling room next to the inbound dock, with a pass-through to raw storage.
- Cleaning equipment and chemicals: I will carve out a separate cleaning utility room adjacent to the high-hygiene area, with no direct opening into product zones.
- Empties route: I will rework the corridor so empties return on the opposite side of the dock, avoiding the finished goods path.

I will update A3 accordingly and share a marked-up version. Before I do, can you confirm the minimum space you need for the sampling room and cleaning store so I do not under-size them?

For sizing:
- Sampling room: minimum 10–12 square meters, enough for a small bench, fridge, and one pallet position. A simple handwash and drain are needed.
- Cleaning store: around 8–10 square meters, with space for chemical cabinets and a floor drain for mixing.

If you can reflect those in A3, I can then check that the flows in A1 and the future SOPs in A6 will fit without awkward workarounds.

On the materials and drainage details you raised:

I had not yet broken down the finishes per zone, so I will add a table into A3 aligned with T8, covering:
- Floors: resin in high-hygiene, sealed concrete in low-risk storage
- Walls: washable coating in production, simpler finish in technical rooms
- Ceilings: smooth, cleanable surfaces in production
- Drainage: target slopes and drain locations

Once that is in place, could you review and confirm what is realistic for T4 and A4? I want to avoid specifying something that later turns out to be unbuildable within our budget.

Yes, once the table is in A3 I can run a quick check against supplier lead times and our budget assumptions in T4.

One request: please also mark which areas are considered high-hygiene versus medium and low. That will help me prioritize where we absolutely need the higher-spec finishes and where we can accept more standard materials.

After that review, I will update A4 with any construction risks and share back here.

Following up on airflow and waste:

- For HVAC, if we can mark supply in the cleanest zones and extraction in corridors and lower-risk areas, we reduce the chance of contaminants moving into production. This will also make it easier later when we define monitoring points in T10.
- For waste, I strongly recommend a direct external door from the waste room, so bins do not travel along the same corridor as staff entering high-hygiene areas.

If these changes are acceptable, I will reflect them as assumptions in the draft of A5 and T5.

Understood. I will:
- Clarify supply and extract points on the HVAC layer in A3 so the direction of air from clean to less clean is explicit.
- Add a direct external door from the waste room and adjust the corridor so it no longer shares the main high-hygiene access.

Once I push the updated A3, could you quickly check that this aligns with your early thinking for A5 so we do not need structural changes later?

One more logistics point before we close this:

For inbound, we will need a small office or desk near the dock for document checks and system entries. It does not need to be big, but if we do not reserve it now, it will end up improvised in a corridor.

For outbound, can we ensure there is enough turning space for pallet jacks and, ideally, a future small forklift? That will influence the width of the outbound corridor and dock area in A3.

If we can accommodate these, I am comfortable aligning T7 with the layout.

Good point. I will add a small dock office near inbound and check corridor widths around outbound to allow for pallet jacks and a future small forklift.

I will incorporate all the feedback into A3 today and share a short summary so we can decide whether this version is ready to move forward for T3 and T8.

I have now updated A3 with the agreed changes:
- Added dedicated sampling room and cleaning store with the requested sizes
- Reworked empties route and outbound path to avoid crossings
- Clarified HVAC supply and extract points and added a direct external waste exit
- Included a finishes table per zone for floors, walls, ceilings, and drainage, aligned with T8
- Marked high, medium, and low hygiene zones and added the dock office and staging areas

From my side, this version is ready to be considered as the baseline layout for T3, pending your final checks.

I have reviewed the updated A3 against the process map in A1.

The sampling room, cleaning store, and revised flows now match what we need for the quality control points defined in T1. I do not see any remaining structural gaps from a quality and food safety flow perspective.

From my side, I am comfortable treating this layout as the reference for finalizing T3 and for drafting the core SOPs in A6.

I have checked the finishes table and drainage layout in A3.

- The proposed resin floors and washable wall finishes in high-hygiene areas are available within our budget and lead times.
- Drainage slopes are achievable with minor adjustments that I can handle in T4 without changing the layout.

I confirm that the materials and finishes for food-contact and high-hygiene areas are acceptable for us to proceed with T4 and T8. I will reflect this in A4 and flag any minor construction risks separately if they appear.

Quick note from logistics: the updated dock and corridor layout in A3 works for the inbound inspection bay and outbound staging we discussed. I will align T7 to this version.

No further comments from my side for the layout decision.

I have rechecked the updated A3 with the airflow and waste changes.

The direction of air from clean to less clean and the direct waste exit address my earlier concerns. I will use this as the spatial basis for the environmental and biological assessment in A5 and the monitoring program in T10.

From my side, I support closing the layout decision on this version.

Recap for this thread:

- We have agreed to use the current A3 as the baseline facility layout and zoning for the new food-grade site, aligned with the process map in A1 and the flow work in T1 and T3.
- Materials and finishes for food-contact and high-hygiene areas, as detailed in A3 and linked to T8, are confirmed as buildable within budget and schedule for T4.

I will now treat this layout as frozen for the tender package, and any further changes will go through a controlled change process so we do not impact the 30-day pilot timeline.

threads.thread_goal: Define and agree on supplier qualification and cold-chain requirements.

messages.text:
I have uploaded the first version of the supplier requirements matrix in A2, covering the scope of T2 and T7.

Structure of A2:
- Tab 1: Supplier qualification criteria (certifications, audit status, specs, traceability)
- Tab 2: Cold-chain handling requirements by material category (temperature ranges, packaging, monitoring)
- Tab 3: Pilot-specific controls and contingency options for higher-risk suppliers, linked to the risk register in A7 and T11

I need your review on two points:
1) Are the minimum quality and documentation requirements for key suppliers sufficient for the new facility?
2) Is the proposed cold-chain monitoring approach during the pilot practical and robust enough?

Please comment directly in A2 or here so we can converge and lock T2 this week.

I have gone through A2, focusing on the qualification criteria.

For key raw material suppliers, I suggest we make the following mandatory for go-live:
- Valid food safety certification (for example, a recognized GFSI scheme) or, if not available, a recent on-site audit report.
- Product specifications including microbiological limits and allergen information.
- Change notification procedure for any process or ingredient changes.

For documentation, could we add a column in A2 to track whether we have received and reviewed each item? That will help us later when we prepare the go-live checklist in A8 and T12.

On cold-chain, the proposed temperature ranges look fine, but I would like to hear from 523303 on any additional biological risk controls we should include.

I have reviewed the cold-chain section in A2 with the risk assessment in mind.

Suggestions:
- For high-risk chilled materials, require continuous temperature logging during transport, with data shared at delivery. Spot checks alone may not be enough.
- For frozen materials, define a maximum allowable time above the target temperature before we classify the shipment as non-conforming.
- For suppliers with a weaker track record, we can add temporary increased sampling on receipt during the pilot.

If we capture these points in A2 and reflect them in A7 and T11 as specific risks and mitigations, I am comfortable that the biological risks are covered for the pilot phase.

From a construction and facility readiness angle, a couple of practical points related to T7 and A4:

- If we require continuous temperature logging, we need to make sure the inbound dock and staging areas have enough power outlets and safe spots for data logger readers.
- For any materials that might need re-cooling on arrival, we should confirm that the cold room capacity and door layout in A3 can handle short-term buffering.

I will note these as dependencies in A4, but I need confirmation from you and 8402 that the operational side can handle the extra checks without slowing down the dock too much.

Good points.

I will update A2 to:
- Make certification or recent audit report mandatory for key suppliers, with a clear exception path documented in A7.
- Add columns to track receipt and review of specs, allergen info, and change notification procedures.

For the go-live checklist in A8 and T12, we can then simply reference the status fields in A2 instead of duplicating work.

On cold-chain, I will incorporate 523303's suggestions and then propose a concrete monitoring approach for the pilot.

I have now adjusted A2 based on your input:
- High-risk chilled: continuous logging required, with data download at delivery.
- Frozen: defined maximum cumulative time above target temperature before rejection.
- Higher-risk suppliers: flagged in A2 with a note to apply increased sampling on receipt during the pilot.

I have also added these as specific entries in A7 and T11 so we can track them as mitigations.

Next question: for the pilot, do we want to apply continuous logging to all chilled suppliers, or only to those in the high-risk category?

For the pilot, I recommend we require continuous logging for all chilled suppliers that deliver materials used directly in the product, not just the highest-risk ones.

This will give us a stronger data set to validate the cold-chain performance early. We can then decide after the pilot whether to relax the requirement for lower-risk suppliers.

If we document this as a pilot-only rule in A2 and A7, it should be manageable.

I agree with applying continuous logging to all chilled suppliers whose materials go into the product during the pilot.

Operationally, we can manage this if we:
- Standardize the data logger check as part of the inbound SOP in A6.
- Include a simple decision tree for what to do when data shows excursions.

I will reflect this in the draft SOPs under T6 so that the dock team has clear instructions.

Understood. I will:
- Mark all relevant chilled suppliers in A2 as requiring continuous logging for the pilot.
- Add a note that this is a pilot rule, to be reviewed after we have enough data.

On the minimum quality and documentation requirements, I have now set the following in A2 as mandatory for key suppliers:
- Certification or recent audit report
- Full product specs including microbiological and allergen data
- Signed change notification commitment

Unless there are objections, I will treat these as the baseline requirements for T2.

On your earlier question about dock operations:

With the SOP support that 8402 mentioned, I think the inbound team can handle the extra data logger checks without major delays, as long as we:
- Have a dedicated spot at the dock for the checks.
- Keep the process simple and standardized.

I will make sure any power and space needs are captured in A4 so we do not miss them during construction.

To summarize the monitoring approach for cold-chain performance during the pilot:

- All chilled suppliers whose materials go directly into the product must use continuous temperature logging during transport.
- Frozen suppliers must respect a defined maximum cumulative time above target temperature, as captured in A2.
- Higher-risk suppliers are flagged for increased sampling on receipt.
- These controls are recorded as mitigations in A7 and tracked in T11.

I propose we adopt this as the agreed monitoring approach for the pilot phase.

From a quality standpoint, I support the monitoring approach you summarized.

With the SOP updates in A6 and T6, and the documentation tracking in A2, we will have enough control and traceability for the pilot.

No further changes requested from my side.

I also agree with the monitoring approach as captured in A2 and A7.

It gives us enough data to validate the cold-chain and react quickly if we see patterns of deviation during the pilot.

I will reference these controls in the environmental and biological risk assessment so that the overall risk picture is consistent.

Closing the loop on this thread:

- We have agreed on the minimum quality and documentation requirements for key suppliers, now captured in A2 and forming the basis of T2.
- We have defined the cold-chain monitoring approach for the pilot, including continuous logging for relevant chilled suppliers and specific rules for frozen materials, recorded in A2, A7, and T11.

I will finalize T2 accordingly and keep A2 as the single source of truth for supplier and cold-chain requirements for the new facility.

threads.thread_goal: Consolidate environmental and biological risk controls into design and SOPs.

messages.text:
I have shared the draft environmental and biological risk assessment in A5, based on the baseline work in T5.

Key preliminary findings:
- External environment: low to moderate risk of airborne contaminants from nearby traffic, higher during peak hours.
- Water: initial samples are within expected ranges, but we should maintain regular monitoring.
- Internal environment: potential hotspots around waste handling, drains, and high-traffic corridors.

I have also outlined proposed mitigations and monitoring points that will feed into T10 and the SOP pack in A6.

I need your input on:
1) Which monitoring points and frequencies we should adopt for go-live.
2) Any design or procedural changes we should implement now, while construction and layout (A3) are still flexible.

Please review A5 and comment so we can converge on a practical, robust set of controls.

I have gone through A5 and the proposed monitoring grid.

For go-live, I suggest we prioritize:
- Weekly environmental swabs in high-hygiene processing areas and adjacent corridors.
- Monthly swabs in raw storage and packaging areas.
- Routine water testing at the main inlet and at least one point in the high-hygiene zone.

We can always scale up if we see issues, but this should be manageable operationally and can be embedded into the SOPs in A6 and T6.

On design, the only immediate concern I see is around drain placement and accessibility for cleaning, which ties back to A3 and T8.

On the design side, looking at A3 against your findings in A5:

- Drains: we have floor drains in all high-hygiene rooms, but I may need to adjust a couple of locations to make them easier to access for cleaning and sampling.
- Air intakes: I will double-check that fresh air intakes are positioned away from the main traffic road to reduce airborne contamination risk.

If you can highlight in A5 which specific areas you consider highest priority for monitoring, I can make sure A3 and T8 reflect that before we finalize.

From construction and commissioning perspective, a few points linked to A4 and T9:

- If we are going to have regular environmental swabs and water tests, we should plan for easy access to sampling points and possibly some wall-mounted holders for sampling kits.
- For drains, we need to ensure the construction method allows for proper sealing and avoids stagnant water.

I will add these as items in A4 so they are checked before we sign off the relevant areas in T9.

Thanks for the concrete proposal.

Your suggested frequencies align well with the risk profile in A5. For go-live, I would refine it slightly:
- High-hygiene processing: weekly swabs for the first three months, then review.
- Adjacent corridors: bi-weekly initially, then monthly if results are stable.
- Raw storage and packaging: monthly is fine.
- Water: monthly at the main inlet and quarterly at the high-hygiene point, unless we see deviations.

I will reflect this in T10 and propose it as the baseline monitoring program for go-live.

For priority areas, based on A5, I would highlight:
- High-hygiene processing rooms, especially near drains and equipment interfaces.
- The transition zones between high-hygiene and other areas.
- The waste room and its immediate surroundings.

If you can ensure in A3 and T8 that drains in these areas are accessible and that we have suitable surfaces for cleaning and sampling, it will make the monitoring program in T10 much more effective.

The refined frequencies you propose are workable from an operations standpoint.

I will integrate them into the draft SOPs in A6 under T6, including:
- Sampling procedures and responsibilities.
- Escalation steps if we see repeated out-of-spec results.

This way, the monitoring program in T10 and the SOPs will be aligned for go-live.

I will adjust A3 and T8 to:
- Reposition a couple of drains in the high-hygiene rooms to make them easier to clean and sample.
- Ensure the transition zones and waste room have appropriate surfaces and access for cleaning and monitoring.

Once updated, I will flag the key sampling points on the layout so you can cross-check with T10.

I have added the sampling access and drain sealing checks into A4 and T9.

During commissioning, we will:
- Verify that drains are installed as per the updated A3 and T8.
- Confirm that sampling points are accessible and clearly marked.

Any issues will be logged and resolved before we sign off those areas for pilot use.

To make this concrete, here is the monitoring program I propose for go-live, based on A5 and our discussion:

- High-hygiene processing: weekly environmental swabs for three months, then review; focus on drains, equipment contact points, and nearby surfaces.
- Transition zones: bi-weekly swabs for three months, then monthly if stable.
- Raw storage and packaging: monthly swabs.
- Water: monthly at main inlet, quarterly at high-hygiene point.

I will formalize this in T10 as the baseline program. Unless there are objections, I suggest we adopt this set of monitoring points and frequencies for go-live.

I support adopting this monitoring program for go-live.

It is consistent with the risk profile in A5 and can be integrated into the SOPs in A6 without overloading the team.

No changes requested from my side.

From a layout perspective, the monitoring program you described fits with the updated A3.

I will make sure the sampling points are clearly indicated on the drawings so that commissioning and operations know exactly where to sample.

I am aligned with the monitoring program and have already added the relevant checks into A4 and T9.

No further comments from construction side.

On additional design and procedural changes to mitigate key risks, based on A5 and our discussion:

Design adjustments:
- Confirm repositioned drains and improved access in high-hygiene and transition areas in A3 and T8.
- Ensure waste room layout supports quick removal and cleaning, with clear separation from clean areas.

Procedural controls:
- Include specific cleaning and disinfection routines for drains and waste areas in the SOPs in A6 and T6.
- Add a simple trigger in the monitoring program in T10 to escalate if we see repeated positives in the same area.

I propose we adopt these design and procedural changes as part of the baseline controls for the new facility.

I agree with incorporating these design and procedural controls.

I will ensure the drain and waste area routines, as well as the escalation triggers, are clearly described in the SOPs in A6 under T6.

I will treat the drain and waste room adjustments you described as mandatory inputs for the finalization of A3 and T8.

Any further changes after this point will need to go through change control so we do not impact schedule.

Recap for this thread:

- We have selected the environmental and biological monitoring points and frequencies for go-live, now captured in T10 and aligned with A5.
- We have agreed on specific design adjustments (drains, waste room, sampling access) in A3 and T8, and procedural controls in A6 and T6 to mitigate key risks.

I will finalize T5 and T10 accordingly and share the updated A5 with these decisions clearly documented.

threads.thread_goal: Lock the commissioning, validation, and pilot go-live plan.

messages.text:
I have posted the draft commissioning and validation plan in A4, covering the scope of T9, and a first pass at the pilot go-live readiness checklist in A8, linked to T12.

Highlights:
- List of systems and equipment to be commissioned: utilities, HVAC, cold rooms, production lines, and key quality equipment.
- Proposed sequence and responsibilities, aligned as much as possible with the layout in A3 and the process map in A1.
- Draft go-live checklist in A8, structured around facility, process, documentation, and training.

I need your review on:
1) Whether the responsibilities and sequence in T9 are realistic and cover all quality and biological checks.
2) Whether the go-live criteria in A8 and T12 are sufficient for a safe pilot start.

Please review and comment so we can converge and lock the plan.

I have reviewed A4 and A8 with the process map in A1 and the flow work in T1 in mind.

Observations:
- Commissioning sequence: utilities and HVAC are correctly placed before high-hygiene room qualification, but we should explicitly include verification of environmental monitoring points from T10 and cleaning validation steps from the SOPs in A6.
- Go-live checklist: the documentation section should reference completion of core SOPs under T6 and training records for operators.

I can help refine the quality-related items in A8 and T12 once we agree on the overall structure.

Looking at A4 from the biological risk angle and cross-checking with A5 and T10:

- I suggest we add a specific step to verify that all environmental and water sampling points are installed and accessible before we start any product-contact commissioning.
- We should also include a short initial monitoring run (for example, one round of swabs and water tests) before pilot production, to confirm the baseline.

If we add these steps into T9 and A4, and reflect them as prerequisites in A8, we will have a more robust start.

From the layout and construction side, reviewing A4 and A8 against A3 and T8:

- The sequence for room readiness looks fine, but we should ensure that any late design tweaks (for example, drains and waste room adjustments) are fully completed and inspected before we start commissioning those areas.
- For the go-live checklist, it might help to include a simple reference to the latest approved version of A3 so that everyone is aligned on what 'ready' means for each area.

I will coordinate with 89804 to make sure the drawings and specs are aligned with the commissioning steps in T9.

From a supply chain and logistics perspective, looking at A4, A8, and the processes in T7 and T11:

- We should include checks that inbound and outbound processes are tested with at least one dry run, including dock scheduling, temperature checks, and documentation flow.
- For the go-live checklist, I recommend adding items to confirm that key suppliers in A2 are fully qualified and that any temporary controls from A7 and T11 are in place.

If we add these, the commissioning plan in T9 will better reflect the end-to-end flow.

Thanks for the feedback.

I will update A4 and T9 to:
- Add explicit steps for verifying environmental monitoring points from T10.
- Include cleaning validation checks aligned with the SOPs in A6.

For A8 and T12, I will add completion of core SOPs and training records as mandatory go-live criteria.

Once I have a revised version, I will share a short summary here.

I will incorporate your suggestions by:
- Adding a commissioning step in A4 and T9 to confirm installation and accessibility of all sampling points.
- Including an initial round of environmental and water tests as a prerequisite before pilot production.

These will also be reflected as required items in A8.

On the logistics side, I will:
- Add dry-run tests for inbound and outbound processes into A4 and T9, including temperature checks and documentation flow.
- Update A8 so that supplier qualification status from A2 and any temporary controls from A7 and T11 are checked before go-live.

This should tie the commissioning plan more closely to the end-to-end flow.

I have now updated A4 and A8 based on all feedback:

- A4 and T9 include steps for utilities, HVAC, room readiness, sampling point verification, initial monitoring run, cleaning validation, and logistics dry runs.
- Responsibilities are assigned to construction, operations, quality, and biology roles for each step.
- A8 and T12 now list go-live criteria across facility, process, documentation, training, supplier readiness, and monitoring.

Please take a quick look and confirm if this integrated schedule and responsibility matrix works for you.

I have rechecked A4 and A8.

The updated plan now clearly includes:
- Verification of monitoring points and initial tests from T10.
- Cleaning validation and SOP completion from A6 and T6.
- Training records and documentation checks.

From a quality and food safety standpoint, the schedule and responsibilities in T9 are acceptable, and the go-live checklist in A8 and T12 covers the key items we need.

I confirm that the updated A4 and A8 reflect the biological controls we discussed:
- Sampling point verification and initial monitoring run.
- Clear prerequisites before any product-contact commissioning.

The responsibilities in T9 are also clear from my side.

I support adopting this integrated commissioning schedule and responsibility matrix.

From supply chain side, the inclusion of inbound and outbound dry runs, and the checks against A2, A7, and T11 in A8, address my earlier concerns.

The timing in T9 is tight but feasible if we keep to the current layout in A3 and avoid late changes.

I am comfortable with the integrated commissioning schedule and responsibilities as drafted.

I have checked that the commissioning steps in A4 and T9 align with the finalized layout and specs in A3 and T8.

No conflicts from my side. I will make sure any remaining minor construction items are closed before the relevant commissioning steps start.

Given the confirmations above, I propose we formally approve the integrated commissioning schedule and responsibilities as defined in A4 and T9.

This will be our reference for tracking progress toward the pilot date.

On the go-live criteria and target date:

Based on the current T9 schedule and the 30-day pilot requirement, I suggest we set the pilot go-live readiness target for day 28, with:
- All items in A8 and T12 completed or formally waived by the relevant stakeholder.
- At least one successful dry run of the end-to-end process, including quality checks.

This gives us a small buffer for any last-minute issues before the actual pilot start.

Day 28 as the readiness target works for supply chain, assuming we keep the current commissioning sequence in T9.

I would only add that any open supplier-related risks in A7 and T11 must have documented temporary controls in place before we call the site ready.

With that condition, I support the proposed go-live criteria and target date.

I am aligned with day 28 as the readiness target, provided that:
- The initial environmental and water monitoring results are within acceptable limits.
- Any deviations have clear corrective actions in place.

These conditions can be captured in A8 and T12 under the biological risk section.

With that, I support the proposed go-live criteria and target date.

Summarizing the go-live criteria and target date based on our discussion:

- Target readiness date: day 28 of the project timeline.
- Criteria: all items in A8 and T12 completed or formally waived; at least one successful end-to-end dry run; supplier risks in A7 and T11 under control; initial environmental and water results acceptable with actions defined for any deviations.

I propose we adopt these as the formal pilot go-live readiness criteria and target date.

I confirm my agreement with the commissioning schedule, responsibilities, and the pilot go-live criteria and target date as summarized.

From quality side, we will now work against A4, A8, T9, and T12 as the reference plan.

Final recap for this thread:

- We have approved the integrated commissioning schedule and responsibilities as defined in A4 and T9.
- We have confirmed the pilot go-live readiness criteria and target date (day 28), as captured in A8 and T12, with links to supplier and risk controls in A7 and T11.

I will now treat these as the baseline for tracking progress toward pilot operations.
